region.text: Where the account is based (canton or country).

model.text: The AI model behind the agent.

expected.text: Whether the check expects a counterexample (a mutant) or none.

outcome.text: Passed or failed against the recorded expectation.

current_step.text: Where the instance stands in its process; written by the loader and dated with the day the instance entered the step (DEC-0018).

ends_on.text: Planned end date; the evaluation runs after it.

keep_threshold.text: The rate at which we keep the approach.

kill_threshold.text: The rate at which we stop it.

metric_key.text: The metric the keep and kill thresholds are set on (reply rate, meeting rate, …).

minimum_sample.text: How many sent before a result counts.

status.text: Planned, running, done, or exploration when the thresholds were not set before the start.

step_history.text: Every step the instance went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader; the flow view measures lead times from it.

variants.text: The A/B variants, if any, as a list.

status.text: How far the capability is: live, on request, built but off, not activated, research or planned.

tier.text: The tier the capability belongs to, or 'to be decided'.

message.text: The first line of the commit message.

pull_request.text: The pull request the commit merged, if any.

alloy_status.text: Whether the component's formal models cover it, as the manifest says.

design_pattern.text: The design pattern the component follows, from its spec (e.g. Facade with Decorator).

display_name.text: The component's human name from the manifest.

docs_status.text: Whether a component folder with README and spec exists.

interactions_source.text: Where the component's calls to other components are declared, or that no source declares any.

source_paths.text: Where the component's code lives, from the manifest.

account_key.text: The account that became this customer.

current_step.text: Where the instance stands in its process; written by the loader and dated with the day the instance entered the step (DEC-0018).

onboarding_state.text: Where the onboarding stands: organisation created, client created, certificate issued, first query.

status.text: Onboarding, active, renewal due, expanded or churned.

step_history.text: Every step the instance went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader; the flow view measures lead times from it.

current_step.text: Where the instance stands in its process; written by the loader and dated with the day the instance entered the step (DEC-0018).

owner.text: Who made or owns the decision.

reversibility.text: Easy, hard or one-way; hard and one-way decisions need a pre-mortem.

status.text: Proposed, reviewed, decided, rejected or superseded.

step_history.text: Every step the instance went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader; the flow view measures lead times from it.

evidence_level.text: Desk research, interview, survey, usage data.

current_step.text: Where the instance stands in its process; written by the loader and dated with the day the instance entered the step (DEC-0018).

keep_threshold.text: The result at which we keep the change.

kill_threshold.text: The result at which we stop.

status.text: Registered, running, decided (keep, kill, iterate) or exploration.

step_history.text: Every step the instance went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader; the flow view measures lead times from it.

current_step.text: Where the instance stands in its process; written by the loader and dated with the day the instance entered the step (DEC-0018).

size_points.text: Estimated size; above the threshold a pre-mortem is required.

status.text: Where the plan stands, from draft to released or killed.

step_history.text: Every step the instance went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader; the flow view measures lead times from it.

substantive_change.text: What changed in the plan's components, invariants, contracts or Alloy models since it was approved; the plan should go back to its brief.

due.text: The date the gate is planned for.

passed_on.text: The date the gate report passed.

not_to_confuse.text: The neighbouring term people mix it up with.

technical_name.text: The name as it appears in the ontology files.

grade.text: 0 to 1 at the end of the period.

owner.text: The role that owns the goal.

how_we_know.text: The observation that would confirm or refute it.

importance.text: Low, high or critical for the business.

contract.text: What the call guarantees, as the interaction catalogue describes it.

methods.text: What the calling component invokes on the other.

protocol.text: How the call travels: in-process, HTTP, a queue, …

documented_in.text: The contract page that describes the route.

infrastructure.text: Whether the route is operational (health, metrics) rather than a product function.

methods.text: The HTTP methods the route accepts.

source_module.text: The code file that registers the route.

area.text: The area of the system the invariant belongs to.

catalog_status.text: Coverage as the catalog page states it (pytest, Alloy, planned).

baseline.text: The value when the goal was set.

metric_key.text: The metric the key result reads.

account_key.text: The account (company) the lead belongs to.

current_step.text: Where the instance stands in its process; written by the loader and dated with the day the instance entered the step (DEC-0018).

persona_key.text: The persona the contact's role maps to.

role_in_deal.text: Economic buyer, champion, user, … (never a name).

segment_key.text: The segment the lead belongs to.

stage.text: New, replied, meeting, opportunity or dropped.

step_history.text: Every step the instance went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader; the flow view measures lead times from it.

computed_from.text: The script or query that computes it; 'asserted' while none exists.

direction.text: Whether up, down or holding steady is good.

target_g4.text: The value the gate G4 must show.

variant.text: The campaign variant the sample belongs to, if any.

account_key.text: The company the deal is with.

buying_centre.text: The roles in the deal mapped to personas, never names.

current_step.text: Where the instance stands in its process; written by the loader and dated with the day the instance entered the step (DEC-0018).

meddpicc_champion.text: Do we have an internal advocate?

meddpicc_competition.text: Do we know what else the customer considers?

meddpicc_decision_criteria.text: Do we know the must-haves and nice-to-haves?

meddpicc_decision_process.text: Do we know who recommends, decides and confirms?

meddpicc_economic_buyer.text: Do we know who holds the budget and signs?

meddpicc_metrics.text: Do we know how the customer measures success?

meddpicc_pain.text: Do we know what it costs the customer to do nothing?

meddpicc_paper_process.text: Do we know the contracts and approvals needed?

next_step.text: What happens next in the deal.

next_step_on.text: When the next step is due.

stage.text: Where the deal stands in the pipeline.

step_history.text: Every step the instance went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader; the flow view measures lead times from it.

value.text: The deal value, as text with currency and period.

version.text: Version and date of the persona sheet.

includes_tier.text: The tier this one builds on.

price_per_user_month.text: The list price, as text with currency.

context.text: What is shown across all steps of a trace: decisions, risks, events that concern the instance (paths as JSON).

exists_today.text: Where the process is written down today.

governing_fact.text: The fact whose value tells an instance's step, e.g. status for a plan or stage for a deal.

instance_types.text: The node types that run through this process.

owner_role.text: The role that defines the process.

pack.text: The pack candidate the concrete process belongs to (engineering, sales and marketing); the generic Process type itself is an EUO candidate.

rules.text: The P-rules the steps of this process use as exit criteria, with their checks, as JSON.

status_map.text: Which step each value of the governing fact stands for, per instance type, as JSON.

transitions.text: The allowed moves between steps as JSON, each marked whether it is rework (a move back).

step_history.text: Every step the case went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader.

exit_criteria.text: Rule ids that must be clean to leave the step (R1–R8 of the rules report, P-rules of the process file).

order.text: Position of the step in the process.

owner_role.text: The role that moves an instance out of this step.

produces.text: The artefacts this step produces, as paths from the instance (JSON); required ones block leaving the step.

requires.text: What must exist before the step can start, as paths from the instance (JSON).

resting.text: Work rests here (decided, released, won …): never reported as stuck.

content_hash.text: A fingerprint of the file, to notice changes.

path.text: Where the file is in the repository.

stale.text: Yes when the ground truth it describes changed or disappeared.

updated_on.text: Last commit date of the file.

current_step.text: Where the instance stands in its process; written by the loader and dated with the day the instance entered the step (DEC-0018).

released_on.text: The date it reached the environment.

step_history.text: Every step the instance went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader; the flow view measures lead times from it.

version.text: The version label of the release.

sample.text: How many the result rests on.

verdict.text: Keep, kill, iterate, or inconclusive below the minimum sample.

current_step.text: Where the instance stands in its process; written by the loader and dated with the day the instance entered the step (DEC-0018).

likelihood_impact.text: Severity as written in the source.

mitigation.text: What is done about it, as written in the plan.

review_date.text: When the risk is re-scored next.

status.text: From identified through owned and mitigating to accepted or closed.

step_history.text: Every step the instance went through with its start and end day, kept by the loader; the flow view measures lead times from it.

holder.text: The person currently holding the role.

actor.text: The agent that ran: the loader, the CI job or an AI agent session.

content_hash.text: A fingerprint of the file, to notice changes.

branches.text: The spine's branches as JSON (e.g. the sales branch of the market spine).

levels.text: The levels as JSON: id, name, types, link to the parent level, verified.

branch.text: main, or the branch the level belongs to.

link_to_parent.text: The relation and direction that link a node here to its parent level.

order.text: Position of the level, top down.

types.text: The node types allowed at this level.

verified.text: Whether an edge of this shape exists on the tenant yet.

line.text: Where it starts in the file.

tests.text: How many tests the module has.

key.text: The stable id of the thing, as it is written in the repository (FEAT-…, L2-…, CAP-…).

last_confirmed.text: When a person last checked that this is still true.

owner.text: The role or person responsible for this thing, as its key (ROLE-…, PERS-…).

owner_text.text: What the source wrote as owner when it names no role or person; the thing has no owner until someone assigns one.

source.text: The file, document or system the node was loaded from.

counterexample.text: A mutant: the check must find a counterexample.

exploration.text: Thresholds not set before the start: counts, not evidence.

live-on-request.text: In production, switched on per request.

precondition.text: Must hold before the component runs.

responsibility.text: What the component is responsible for.

certificate-issued.text: The client holds its mTLS certificate.

first-query.text: The customer ran its first query.

organisation-created.text: The organisation exists in the admin console.

hard.text: Expensive to undo; needs a pre-mortem.

one-way.text: Cannot be undone; needs a pre-mortem.

exploration.text: No thresholds set in advance: not evidence.

cut-scope.text: A tripwire fired and scope was cut.

value.text: An allowed value of an enum attribute.

no.text: A route that offers a product function.

yes.text: An operational route such as /health or /metrics.

qualified.text: Worth pursuing (economic buyer and pain known).

explanation.text: Why things are as they are.

how-to.text: Steps to get a task done.

iterate.text: Between the thresholds: change and run again.

kill.text: At or below the kill threshold.

avoid.text: Change course so it cannot happen.

no.text: No edge of this shape yet; expect it empty.

about.sentence: Goal is about Capability — the goal concerns this capability, segment or process.

accepted_by.sentence: Risk was accepted by Role — this role decided to live with the risk.

advanced_by.sentence: Process instance was advanced by Event — this event moved it to the next step.

affects.sentence: Decision affects Component — the decision changes this part of the software or this plan.

blocked_by.sentence: Feature plan is blocked by Decision — the plan cannot proceed until this is decided.

calls.sentence: Component calls Component — the first invokes the second; read backwards it is called-by.

calls_back.sentence: Component calls back Component — it calls a component that also calls it; read like calls.

changes.sentence: Commit changes Component — the change touched files of this component.

converts_to.sentence: Lead converts to Account — the sales branch moves forward one stage.

decided_by.sentence: Decision was decided by Person — this person or role made the call.

defines.sentence: Source file defines Symbol — the class or function lives in this file.

depends_on.sentence: Component depends on Component — it cannot work without the other.

describes.sentence: Record describes Component — this document is about this part.

evidenced_by.sentence: Hypothesis is evidenced by Evidence record — this evidence speaks for the claim.

examines.sentence: Pre-mortem examines Feature plan — this session looked at how the plan could fail.

exposes.sentence: Component exposes Interface — the component serves this route.

for_account.sentence: Opportunity is for Account — the deal, lead, customer, quote or contract belongs to this company.

gated_by.sentence: Phase is gated by Gate — the phase ends only when this gate passes.

governs.sentence: Component contract governs Component — this clause applies to this component.

has_key_result.sentence: Goal has key result Key result — this number shows whether the goal moved.

has_level.sentence: Spine has level Spine level — this level belongs to the spine, in order.

has_step.sentence: Process has step Process step — this state belongs to the process.

held_by.sentence: Role is held by Person — this person currently wears the hat.

implements.sentence: Commit implements Feature plan — this change is part of carrying out the plan.

in_market.sentence: Segment is in market Market — this customer type belongs to this market.

in_state.sentence: Decision is in state Process step — where the case stands today.

initiated_by.sentence: Interaction is initiated by Component — the calling side.

instance_of.sentence: Feature plan is an instance of Process — this plan runs through this process.

justified_by.sentence: Feature plan is justified by Hypothesis — we build it because we believe this about customers.

keeps.sentence: Component keeps Invariant — this component must uphold this invariant.

measured_by.sentence: Campaign is measured by Metric — the keep and kill thresholds are set on this metric.

measures.sentence: Key result measures Metric — the key result is read from this metric.

member_of.sentence: Persona belongs to Segment — this persona works at this kind of customer; a role belongs to a function.

mitigated_by.sentence: Risk is mitigated by Feature plan — this work reduces the risk.

motivated_by.sentence: Feature plan is motivated by Goal — the plan exists because of this goal.

observed_in.sentence: Hypothesis was observed in Evidence record — the claim showed up in this evidence.

offers.sentence: Tier offers Capability — management says this tier (or API group) sells this capability.

owned_by.sentence: Goal is owned by Role — this role is responsible for it.

part_of.sentence: Component is part of Software area — the component belongs to this area; a tier is part of the product, a function of the company, a process of its value stream.

performed_by.sentence: Event was performed by Agent — this actor did it.

produced.sentence: Campaign produced Lead — this reply came out of the campaign.

raised_in.sentence: Risk was raised in Pre-mortem — the risk came out of this session.

realises.sentence: Component realises Capability — engineering says this part of the software delivers this capability.

received_by.sentence: Interaction is received by Component — the called side.

related.sentence: X is related to Y — the API's default when no better relation was named; reported by rule 0.

results_in.sentence: Experiment results in Decision — the experiment ended in this outcome or decision.

reworks_to.sentence: Process step reworks to an earlier Process step — the instance goes back for rework, e.g. an approved plan back to its brief.

satisfies.sentence: Component contract satisfies Invariant — this clause is how the component upholds the invariant.

serves.sentence: Feature plan serves Capability — the plan exists to deliver or improve this capability.

supersedes.sentence: Decision supersedes Decision — the newer one replaces the older one, which stays on record.

targets.sentence: Hypothesis targets Persona — the claim is about this persona or segment; a campaign targets a segment.

tests.sentence: Experiment tests Hypothesis — the experiment or campaign is designed to confirm or refute it.

threatens.sentence: Risk threatens Goal — if the risk happens, this goal is in danger.

touches.sentence: Event touches Feature plan — the event concerned this thing.

transitions_to.sentence: Process step transitions to Process step — the allowed next state.

uses.sentence: Campaign uses Marketing asset — the campaign sends this one-pager, deck or mail.

verifies.sentence: Alloy check verifies Invariant — this check proves the invariant holds; a test run verifies a plan or component.

via.sentence: Campaign via Channel — the campaign runs through this channel.

Agent.text: An automated actor such as a Claude Code session or a scheduled job that reads and proposes in the brain.

AlloyCheck.confuse: A test run executes code; an Alloy check proves a property of a model.
AlloyCheck.text: One formal check of a system model (Alloy) recorded in the lockfile; it verifies a component or an invariant.

ApiServiceGroup.confuse: A platform tier is what end users buy; a service group is what developers integrate.
ApiServiceGroup.example: API-SEARCH, everything about searching with cited passages.
ApiServiceGroup.text: A grouping of the Knovas API as software vendors and partners see it (Ingest, Search, Graph, …). A proposal in Phase 0.

BoundedContext.confuse: A capability describes what a customer can do, not how the software is split.
BoundedContext.example: L1-RETRIEVE, everything about search and retrieval.
BoundedContext.text: One of the nine large areas the Knovas software is divided into; each has its own responsibility and vocabulary and contains several components (L2).

Campaign.confuse: An experiment is the general type; a campaign is the marketing kind of it and appears on the same board.
Campaign.example: CMP-2026-11-icp01-head-of-dev, a call campaign to 40 ICP-01 heads of development.
Campaign.text: A marketing effort aimed at a segment and its personas, run as a registered experiment: it tests a persona hypothesis with a metric, a minimum sample and keep and kill thresholds set before it starts.

Capability.confuse: A component is a part of the software; a capability says what the customer gets, not how it is built.
Capability.example: CAP-06, file a document to the right client and matter.
Capability.text: One thing a customer can do with Knovas, in plain words. It is the meeting point between what management sells and what engineering builds.

Channel.text: How a segment is reached: direct, resellers, software vendors, events, content.

Commit.example: COMMIT-215b05af5f77, the merge of Client Zero Phase 0.
Commit.text: One recorded change to a repository, linked to the plan it implements and the components it touched.

Company.confuse: An account is a customer company; the company is Knovas.
Company.text: The company itself, root of the organisation spine.

Component.confuse: A source file is a single code file; a component is the unit engineers own and document.
Component.example: L2-KNOWLEDGE-GRAPH, the knowledge graph the brain is built on.
Component.text: A part of the Knovas software with a clear responsibility, its own documentation and tests, inside one software area.

ComponentContract.confuse: An invariant holds for the whole system; a contract belongs to one component.
ComponentContract.example: L2-KNOWLEDGE-GRAPH/POST-P0-01, new chunks carry the access scope of their document from the moment they exist.
ComponentContract.text: A promise a component makes: what must be true before it runs (precondition), what is true afterwards (postcondition), or what it is responsible for.

Contract.example: A reseller contract with a 25 % margin.
Contract.text: A signed agreement with a customer or partner.

Customer.example: A pilot law firm in its first 90 days.
Customer.text: An account that signed, from onboarding through renewal, expansion or churn.

Decision.confuse: A goal says where to go; a decision says which way was chosen.
Decision.example: DEC-0001, Client Zero runs on tenant af639810.
Decision.text: A recorded choice with its date, who made it, what it affects and what it replaces, moving from proposed to decided.

Deployment.example: The brain MVP on cloudscale prod, 24 Oct 2026.
Deployment.text: A release of the software to an environment on a date.

Event.confuse: A run event only records that the loader, CI or an agent ran; it is bookkeeping, not business.
Event.example: A decision review that touches PROC-decision (the G2 ritual).
Event.text: Something that happened in the business at a time, done by a person, touching one or more things in the brain: a decision review held, a step entered, a campaign ended.

EvidenceRecord.example: EV-0001, Explorium data on DACH software vendors.
EvidenceRecord.text: A piece of evidence for or against a hypothesis: an interview, a statistic, a source.

Experiment.example: EXP-stage-0-probe, does concept membership beat the cheap null on German legal text?
Experiment.text: A registered test of a hypothesis with keep and kill thresholds set before it starts and an end date.

FeaturePlan.confuse: A decision is one choice inside or around a plan; a plan is the whole piece of work.
FeaturePlan.example: FEAT-2026-10-25-client-zero-phase-0, the plan for Phase 0 of Client Zero.
FeaturePlan.text: The written plan for a piece of work: what problem it solves, which components it changes, which contracts and invariants apply, and its status from draft to released.

Function.text: A part of the company such as research, engineering, sales or finance.

Gate.confuse: A milestone is a date something is due; a gate is a test that must pass.
Gate.example: G1, every component, plan and invariant exists as a node and one feature is traced to its commits.
Gate.text: A checkpoint at the end of a phase with a pass criterion the brain itself can check; the next phase starts only when it passes.

GlossaryTerm.text: One entry of this glossary inside the brain: a type, attribute, relation or value with its plain-language description.

Goal.confuse: A key result is the number that shows the goal moved; a goal is the outcome.
Goal.example: GOAL-2026-Q4-client-zero-foundation, Knovas steers itself from its own brain by G1.
Goal.text: What must change by the end of a month or a quarter, owned by a role, measured by key results.

Hypothesis.confuse: An experiment is the test; a hypothesis is the claim being tested.
Hypothesis.example: P-02.H01, an associate loses at least one hour per day searching for prior work.
Hypothesis.text: A belief about customers or the product that has not been proven yet, with a status from asserted to validated or refuted.

Interaction.confuse: An interface is the entry point; an interaction is who calls whom through it.
Interaction.example: IX-L2-SECURE-API--L2-QUERY-2STAGE, the Secure API passing a search to the two-stage query engine.
Interaction.text: One software component calling another: which methods, over which protocol, under which contract.

Interface.confuse: A capability is what a customer can do; an interface is one technical entry point.
Interface.example: IF-secure_api:/secured/query, the search route of the Secure API.
Interface.text: An HTTP route a software component serves, with its methods and the page that documents it; read from the code.

Invariant.confuse: A component contract is local to one part; an invariant is system-wide.
Invariant.example: GI-GRAPH-13, document sorting only ever proposes; the client decides.
Invariant.text: A rule the whole system must keep at all times, written down with an id, verified by tests and formal checks.

KeyResult.example: KR-plan-coverage-g1, approved plans that satisfy rule 1, from 0 % to 90 %.
KeyResult.text: A measurable target on one metric that shows whether a goal was reached: baseline, target and actual value.

Lead.confuse: An opportunity is a qualified deal with a stage; a lead is the first reply.
Lead.example: LEAD-cmp-2026-11-icp01-acc-0007, economic buyer (P-03) at account ACC-0007.
Lead.text: A company that showed interest in a campaign, stored as the account plus the buying-centre role mapped to a persona, never as a name or contact detail (privacy rule).

Market.example: MKT-01, DACH, the True Graph company brain.
Market.text: A region and offering Knovas sells into.

MarketingAsset.text: A one-pager, deck, demo or case study written for a persona.

Metric.confuse: A metric sample is one measured value at a time; the metric is the definition.
Metric.example: MET-staleness, the share of canonical records flagged stale.
Metric.text: A named, computable measure with a unit and a direction (up or down is better).

MetricSample.text: One measured value of a metric at a point in time, computed by a script, never typed by hand.

Milestone.example: MS-CORTEX-DEFAULT, Cortex is the default module in every law-firm deal.
Milestone.text: A dated point in a plan, such as a launch or a contract, by which something must be done.

Opportunity.example: A proof of concept with a Treuhand firm, stage quote.
Opportunity.text: A deal in the sales pipeline with its stage and its MEDDPICC qualification.

Person.text: A named person at Knovas (no private data beyond the name).

Persona.example: P-10, the senior lawyer who is the practice group's memory.
Persona.text: An archetype of a person in the buying centre of a customer, with pains, goals and a role in the deal.

Phase.example: Phase 1 of Client Zero, ground truth, ended with gate G1 on 25 Oct 2026.
Phase.text: A dated stretch of a plan that ends at a gate.

PlatformTier.confuse: An API service group groups the same capabilities for software vendors; it is not a tier.
PlatformTier.example: TIER-CORTEX, Core plus a simple brain, CHF 59.90 per user and month.
PlatformTier.text: One of the three cumulative levels of the Platform that a customer buys: Core, Cortex or Nexus. Each includes the one before it.

PreMortem.example: PM-client-zero-2026-10-24, eight ways Client Zero could fail by March 2027.
PreMortem.text: A session before a big plan or decision in which the team assumes it already failed and writes down why; it produces risks and tripwires.

Process.confuse: A process instance is one run of it; the process is the definition.
Process.example: PROC-decision, proposed, reviewed, decided or rejected, superseded.
Process.text: How a kind of work moves: its steps and the allowed transitions, with an owner.

ProcessInstance.example: The Client Zero Phase 0 plan as an instance of the feature lifecycle, currently approved.
ProcessInstance.text: One running case of a process, such as one feature moving through the feature lifecycle.

ProcessStep.text: One named state of a process.

Product.confuse: A platform tier (Core, Cortex, Nexus) is a level within the Platform product, not a product of its own.
Product.text: Something Knovas sells as a whole: the Platform for end users or the API for software vendors.

Quote.example: 20 Cortex seats for a law firm.
Quote.text: A priced offer: articles, seats, API buckets.

Record.confuse: A source file is the code itself; a record describes it.
Record.text: A human-written description of how things are: a README, a spec, a glossary page, a runbook. It must point at the ground truth it describes and is flagged stale when that changes.

Release.confuse: A deployment is one rollout to one environment; a release is the versioned whole that may be deployed to dev and then prod.
Release.example: REL-2026.10-brain-mvp, the brain MVP on cloudscale prod, 24 Oct 2026.
Release.text: A versioned release of the software moving from candidate through verified and deployed to announced; recorded by the engine owner in releases.yaml because no git tag or deploy flow marks releases today.

Repository.text: A git repository holding code or documents.

Result.text: The measured outcome of an experiment or campaign, with the verdict the evaluation proposes.

Risk.confuse: A tripwire is the threshold that triggers action; a risk is what might happen.
Risk.example: RISK-01, capacity: two founders plus thesis and research probe.
Risk.text: Something that could go wrong, with an owner, a review date and either a mitigation or an explicit acceptance.

Role.confuse: A persona is a customer archetype used in sales, not a role at Knovas.
Role.text: A hat a person wears, such as ontology steward or engine owner; roles own things, people hold roles.

RunEvent.confuse: An event is a business fact such as a decision taken or a step entered; a run event only records that a script or agent ran.
RunEvent.example: EVT-loader-2026-10-27-195507-646946, a loader run that moved four plans.
RunEvent.text: A bookkeeping record of one loader, CI or agent run: when it ran, who ran it and which plans, decisions, risks and components it changed. Instance views hide run events as a whole.

Segment.confuse: A persona is a person inside such a customer; a segment is the company type.
Segment.example: ICP-03, law firms in Switzerland and Germany.
Segment.text: A kind of customer Knovas targets, the ideal customer profile.

SourceFile.text: One code or model file in a repository, with a content hash so changes are noticed.

Spine.confuse: A process says how work moves through steps; a spine says how things are arranged under each other.
Spine.example: SPINE-product: product → tier → capability → software area → component → sub-part.
Spine.text: An ordered list of levels — a type at each level and the relation that links it to the level above — along which the company's things hang: product, organisation, process, market. The Platform draws trees and matrices from it.

SpineLevel.example: SPINE-product/L3, the capability level, linked to its tier by offers.
SpineLevel.text: One level of a spine: the node types allowed there and the relation to the parent level.

Symbol.text: A class, function or method inside a source file.

System.confuse: A product is what Knovas sells; the system is the software that runs it.
System.text: The Knovas software as a whole; its software areas are part of it, and its reference documentation starts here.

TestRun.text: The result of running one test module on a date: passed or failed, how many tests.

Tripwire.example: TW-g1-no-trace, no feature traceable end to end at G1 means fix ingestion first.
Tripwire.text: A threshold on a metric that forces a decision when it fires.

ValueStream.confuse: A process is one flow of steps; a value stream groups several.
ValueStream.example: VS-build: feature lifecycle, decision, risk review, release.
ValueStream.text: A group of processes that together deliver one kind of value, root of the process spine.

report_rules.description: Every node has a key fact; relations come from relations.yaml and respect domain and range; numbers are text with a unit; type descriptions carry the [level=…] header.
report_rules.name: Conventions

report_rules.description: An approved plan has an owner, affects at least one component, serves a capability and is motivated by a goal or justified by a hypothesis.
report_rules.name: Approved plan is complete

report_rules.description: An implemented or released plan has at least one implementing commit and at least one passing test run or Alloy check from CI (local runs are not evidence).
report_rules.name: Done means evidenced

report_rules.description: A decision names what it affects, has an owner and, once decided, a date; a superseded one names its successor.
report_rules.name: Decision is complete

report_rules.description: A risk has an owner and a review date, and an open risk has a mitigation or an explicit acceptance.
report_rules.name: Risk is handled

report_rules.description: A record describes something or is evidence for it, and is not stale.
report_rules.name: Record is linked and fresh

report_rules.description: An L2 component resolves to an existing source path; an invariant has a passing Alloy check from CI or a decided decision covering it.
report_rules.name: Ground truth resolves

report_rules.description: A large plan (50 sp or more), a quarterly goal or a hard-to-reverse decision is examined by a pre-mortem that raised at least one risk and one tripwire.
report_rules.name: Pre-mortem before big bets

report_rules.description: Every type, attribute, relation and enum value has a description in descriptions.yaml.
report_rules.name: Plain-language descriptions

rules.description: Registered before the start: thresholds and the minimum sample are set (goal rule 3); an `exploration` instance fails this on purpose.
rules.name: Keep and kill thresholds set

context_packs.description: A plan and its components, contracts, invariants, open decisions and risks, each with the file it is defined in.

agent.description: An agent implementing one plan: gets everything the plan needs and nothing more; every output is a proposal a person accepts.

ci.description: The CI job that reads the rules report and, once out of report mode, fails a merge that adds a new rule violation.

cto.description: Sees and steers the whole software: what it consists of, what is planned and done, which decisions and risks sit where, and how healthy the knowledge is.

definition.description: Software areas → components → interfaces, each component coloured by its documentation completeness and the status of the checks on its invariants.
One plan from left to right: the components it changes, the invariants it keeps, the checks that verify them, the commits that implement it and the release that shipped them.
Every feature plan in the column of its feature-lifecycle step, with what is missing to leave the step.
Decisions newest first, with what each affects, its state, and whether a pre-mortem examined it.
Open risks grouped by component: the component's own risks and those of the plans that affect it.
Per type of health.yaml: correctness, completeness and compliance (DC-34), with the owner role and the review rhythm.
